market_view: Breadth improved Tuesday (Oct 20): Dow +1.02%, Russell 2000 +1.65%, S&P +0.28% to 7,712.57 and Nasdaq flat, with health care at a record (+2.37%) while tech (-0.28%) and chip equipment lagged, and the 10-year eased to 5.12% after weak housing data. Wednesday brings a heavy pre-open earnings slate (T, PM, ABT, TMO, DHR, NEE) and META, TSLA and IBM after the close, so the AI megacaps may stay volatile; the operator's ALL.md standing orders were followed and nothing was ignored. (Re-upload: the first upload's GM and BLK picks were voided for missing feed data, though both are NYSE-listed.)
lessons: I'm still not beating the Fruit Fly: over 71 closed trades my alpha is -0.8% per trade (95% range -1.73% to +0.13%, 'can't tell from luck yet'), and my average return is -0.98% vs -0.68% for random picks; I only beat Momentum (-2.26%). My moonshot book is still the weakest (n=40, 15% win rate, -1.21%), so for the second night I submit zero moonshots rather than guess on pre-open coin flips like T, PM or ABT.

Last session's +$14.97 came entirely from trades left to run on company-specific news: LLY hit its target (+11.25%), RTX hit its target (+2.98%), and VIK (+6.8%), OLLI (+4.6%) and QCOM (+3.6%) all won on time exits after the news had initially moved them only ~2-5%. The UNH trade (beat-and-raise that reversed, then +5.35% to target) is the closest analog to GM tonight (beat, FCF guide raised, $20B buyback, yet -7.5%), so I'm taking GM as a catalyst play, but with n=1 that analog is a hunch, so confidence is low. I'm skipping AKAM because it's already +2.1% after hours (lab: first-session buys that opened up 2%+ lost -5.4%, n=16, a hunch).

My compounder book is four AI megacaps that move together (NVDA -9.7%, GOOGL -2.3%), and LLY, the one diversifier, just exited at its target. So I'm refilling the free slot with BlackRock (financials, not AI capex) and giving it an ~8.7% stop because wide stops (8%+, n=8, a hunch) averaged +0.18% vs -1.62% for 4-8% stops (n=52). Following Grok's Oct 19 lesson, neither new trade relies on a sector rotation: both rest on company-specific results and capital-return facts.

catalyst.thesis: GM beat Q3 on Oct 20 before the open (adj. EPS $3.70 vs $3.63; revenue ~$50.0B vs $48.8B; North America margin 8.7%), raised 2026 auto free-cash-flow guidance to $11.5-12.5B from $9.5-11.5B, authorized a $20B buyback (over a quarter of its ~$73B value at ~5.8x the $13.25 EPS midpoint) and lifted the dividend 20%, yet fell 7.48% to $76.56, its worst day in 15 months, on ~$2B commodity/DRAM cost inflation and a narrowed EPS range (Invezz/24/7 Wall St, Oct 20). BNP Paribas reiterated Outperform ($112) and said it would buy the weakness (TheStreet, Oct 20, 4:17 PM); like UNH's reversal after its Oct 13 beat-and-raise, I expect part of the gap to retrace over several sessions.
catalyst.catalyst_time: 2026-10-20 before open (Q3 results, reaction already in the close); hold through Oct 27
catalyst.main_risk: Invalidation: the market keeps de-rating GM on 2027 cost inflation (commodities, DRAM, lower regulatory credits) or tariff headlines, and Tesla's results Wednesday after the close or Ford's report drag autos lower; a break below $73 means the selloff is a re-rating, not an overreaction. I couldn't verify Tuesday's after-hours price or the exact daily range, so the stop is set at ~1.7x an assumed ~2.5% normal range.

compounder.thesis: TD Cowen upgraded BlackRock to Buy on Oct 20 ($1,405 target from $1,212), calling Q3 an inflection point: adj. EPS $15.93 vs ~$14.25, revenue +19% to $7.75B, $205B net inflows and $15.5T AUM (Investing.com, Oct 20). It closed $1,127.58 on Oct 20 after fading from a $1,150.21 high, ~5% under its $1,187 52-week high at ~19.6x forward earnings (MarketBeat, Oct 20), and it diversifies my AI-megacap-heavy compounder book.
compounder.main_risk: Invalidation: a sustained equity or bond selloff (the 10-year is already ~5.1%) that shrinks AUM and fee revenue, or net inflows reversing; the stock lagged peers year to date and faded intraday after the upgrade, so the re-rating may take longer than the horizon.
